title: Leakage-aware width right-sizing (uniform channel width, from scratch)
question: How much detector width is required when model selection uses source-INDEPENDENT rather than source-exposed performance?
scope_note: Separately authorised deployment/right-sizing study. The Phase 12-14 mechanism search stays closed. No new module of any kind in this phase.
architecture_rule: Depth and topology identical; only the YOLO11n width multiplier changes.
initialisation: Random initialisation for ALL four widths, including 1.00x. No pretrained tensor is loaded (yaml-built model, pretrained=False). Rationale: pretrained transfer is 98.21% / 7.94% / 15.22% / 22.93% of params for 1.00x / 0.75x / 0.50x / 0.35x and would confound width with initialisation quality.
seed_rule: Same five seeds for every width. No seed added post hoc to any width.

training.source: configs/experiments.yaml [train], identical to runs_p4/r512 except init

schedule_gate: Before step 1 of every run the trainer's computed schedule (steps/epoch, epochs, total updates, warmup updates, mosaic-close epoch) must equal runs_p4/r512/seed0/schedule.json, else the run aborts (exit 3).
init_gate: Before training, every run checks (a) built params == audited params and (b) for w100, the first conv weight differs from yolo11n.pt (no silent pretrained load).
test_access: NONE. The clean test split is not read by any Phase 15 script.

evaluation.arms: Phase 9 frozen arms over the official-val union (2439 images): arm B = source-INDEPENDENT (213 families, 411 files), arm A = source-EXPOSED (1047 families, 2028 files). Manifests/hashes: phase9/arm_freeze_record.json.
evaluation.inference: imgsz 512, conf 0.001, NMS IoU 0.7, max_det 300, top-100 per image
evaluation.scorer: pycocotools COCO AP@[.50:.95], maxDets 100, 8 categories (as Phase 9/12)
evaluation.decomposition: Phase 12 matching rules: conf 0.25, greedy one-to-one class-agnostic match at IoU 0.50; strict 0.75
evaluation.also: clean-val (268 originals) Ultralytics val at every checkpoint, descriptive only

primary_endpoint: six-class AP50-95 on arm B (source-independent) at 24570 updates

primary_test.hypotheses: H0(w): mean Delta(w) <= -1.5  vs  H1(w): mean Delta(w) > -1.5, w in {w075,w050,w035}
primary_test.test: one-sided paired t, df=4: t = (mean Delta + 1.5) / SE
primary_test.multiplicity: Holm step-down across the three reduced-width comparisons, familywise alpha 0.05 (one-sided).
primary_test.rule: w is NON-INFERIOR iff its Holm-adjusted one-sided p < 0.05 AND its multiplicity-adjusted one-sided lower confidence bound > -1.5, where the bound for the hypothesis at Holm rank k (k=1 smallest p) uses level alpha/(3-k+1); a Bonferroni alpha/3 simultaneous bound is also reported as the conservative check. Testing stops at the first non-rejected rank (standard Holm).
primary_test.interpretation_guard: Failure to establish non-inferiority is NOT evidence of inferiority and is reported as 'non-inferiority not established'.
primary_test.margin_rationale: Median paired 5-seed SD of arm-B AP differences across the 45 existing Phase 9 model pairs is 0.84 AP; at +/-1.0 equivalence would only be attainable for |mean diff| < 0.20. Margin -1.5 specified by the user before any Phase 15 run.
primary_test.not_evidence: A non-significant difference is never reported as equivalence.

secondary_tests.tost_equivalence: two-sided TOST at +/-1.5 AP, paired t df=4, per width vs w100, Holm over 3 widths
secondary_tests.trajectories: all four checkpoints + per-epoch clean-val curves, descriptive
secondary_tests.superiority: one-sided paired t that w > w100 on arm B, Holm over 3 widths (Outcome D screen)
secondary_tests.family_bootstrap: 1000 resamples of source families (arms A and B independently, all files of a family together); paired seed-mean Delta and interaction per width

secondary_endpoints: six-class AP50, AP75, APs, AR100 (A and B)
class-agnostic AP50-95, AP50, AP75 (A and B)
false positives per family (A and B)

exposure_interaction.I: Delta_ind - Delta_exp, per seed; paired t + family bootstrap

convergence_diagnostic.flag: w is 'still improving' iff mean g(w) > 0.5 AP AND one-sided paired t p < 0.05
convergence_diagnostic.consequence: A flagged width is reported as FIXED-BUDGET performance, never as an asymptotic capacity limit.
convergence_diagnostic.extension_rule: No schedule extension inside Phase 15. Any extension is a new, separately frozen phase that must apply the same longer schedule to ALL four widths. No rescue training of any single width.

resource_note: GPU speed-up is claimed only if measured. Untrained timing 8.90 ms (0.35x) vs 9.13 ms (1.00x) at batch 16 is treated as no meaningful latency gain.
decision_rule: Among reduced widths that pass corrected non-inferiority, select the SMALLEST by parameter count. If none pass, report the observed accuracy-size Pareto frontier without claiming preserved accuracy.
integrity_rules: The clean test split is not inspected during development.
The margin and all rules are not changed after any result is seen.
Best-validation checkpoints are never the primary outcome; the primary is the fixed 24570-update checkpoint.
No edge-device speed claim is made from desktop GPU timings.

decision_rules.A: w035 non-inferior -> select 0.35x; STOP architecture experimentation.
decision_rules.B: w050 non-inferior, w035 not -> frontier lies between 0.35x and 0.50x; authorise design of ONE matched-budget localization-preserving asymmetric-width candidate (separate frozen phase).
decision_rules.C: w050 not non-inferior -> report the Pareto frontier; architecture work only with a mechanism-based budget-redistribution hypothesis; no module invention.
decision_rules.D: any narrower width superior to w100 on arm B (Holm one-sided p < 0.05) -> report as a capacity-generalization result and test whether arm A gives the opposite sign. D can co-occur with A/B/C.
